title: Hotfix: prevent failover controller NPE when a signal stream is missing
author: Benji Okafor
description:
Context: During staging rehearsal for regional failover automation, the failover controller crashed with a nil pointer dereference when one of the signal streams (capacity/headroom) was absent for a subset of regions/routes. This can happen during partial outages of the signal publisher, misconfigured routing configs in staging, or when a region is newly added and the signal pipeline hasn’t started publishing yet. The controller should degrade safely (no action + clear evidence) rather than crash-loop.

What changed: 1) Make signal reads total: convert all signal fetch paths in the controller to return an explicit tri-state (present/absent/stale) instead of a nil map/struct. Missing signals no longer cause an NPE. 2) Deterministic behavior on missing inputs: if a signal required for corroboration (per ADR-042) is missing, the controller marks the evaluation as `insufficient_evidence` and produces a no-op plan; we do not flip policies based on partial evidence. If the missing signal is non-authoritative for the decision path, we proceed but record `missing_signal_sources` on the evaluation log/audit event. 3) Observability: add `failover_controller_missing_signal_total{signal=<name>,region=<region>}` counter and emit a structured log + audit event annotation when a required stream is missing for >2 evaluation intervals. 4) Safety: add a short circuit to avoid writing partial plans when evaluation errors occur; controller returns a stable empty plan and increments `failover_controller_eval_errors_total`.

Tests: Adds a regression test that reproduces the panic (signal store returns absent for a configured signal). Adds table-driven tests for the new evaluation contract (required vs optional signals) and verifies the controller produces a no-op plan and emits the missing-signal metric/log.

Impact/Risk: Low functional risk (hotfix + behavior only affects missing-signal cases). This reduces the chance of controller crash-loop during impairment, and avoids acting on incomplete evidence.

Rollout: Merge to main and deploy to staging immediately. After 30 minutes of stable evaluations (no panic, expected metric increments only), promote to production via standard controller rollout (helm chart values unchanged; behavior is code-only). On-call notes included below.
commits: failover/controller: represent signal fetch as Present/Absent/Stale + remove nil deref path
failover/controller: treat missing required corroboration as insufficient_evidence (no-op plan)
observability: add missing-signal counter + log fields for evaluation evidence
tests: regression reproducer for missing signal stream + table-driven evaluation cases
docs: update controller troubleshooting section (missing signals / evidence) in runbook snippet
conversation: Miles Thornton (review): Can we confirm we never flip when a required corroboration signal is missing? I want this to be strictly safer than before.
Benji Okafor (author): Yes. `required=true` signals now gate the evaluation: we return `insufficient_evidence` and emit a no-op plan. Added test `TestEvaluator_MissingRequiredSignal_NoOpPlan`.
Jordan Lee (review): Please ensure this doesn't introduce hidden oscillation if signals flap between absent/present. Do we have any dampening on the 'missing required signal' state itself?

Benji Okafor (author): We don't change routing when absent; the controller keeps existing policy state. For noise, we only alert/annotate after >2 consecutive intervals missing (see `missingSignalHoldDown=2`).
Allison Grant (review): Metric label cardinality: please avoid route/model labels. Region + signal is fine. Also add log field listing which sources were missing.
Benji Okafor (author): Updated metric to only include {signal, region}. Added `missing_signal_sources` array in structured logs (no route/model).
Rafael Mendes (review): Add a note in rollout steps for on-call: what to look for in dashboards and how to verify no panic-loop.
Benji Okafor (author): Added rollout notes + suggested queries to the PR description and troubleshooting doc.
rollout_notes: Staging: Deploy immediately after merge. Verify `failover-controller` pod restarts == 0 and `failover_controller_eval_errors_total` remains flat. If testing missing-signal behavior, expect `failover_controller_missing_signal_total{signal="capacity_headroom"}` to increment for the affected region(s), and controller should keep emitting no-op plans (no policy writes). Production: Standard rolling deploy. No feature flags required. If `missing_signal_total` spikes in prod, treat as signal pipeline issue (not routing); do not attempt manual failover based on incomplete evidence—follow runbook troubleshooting section 'Missing signal streams'.
release_notes: Reliability: Failover controller no longer crash-loops when a signal stream is missing; missing required corroboration signals result in safe no-op decisions with improved metrics/logging for triage.
